correctness.rationale: For every prime p=10n+1>13 the complete Kummer differential basis has character dimensions (0,1,2,3). Direct Cartier coefficient extraction gives B2 a unit times lambda^n Q_n, B3 diagonal with one universally nonzero factor and one Q_n factor, while the third character component of height and dimension three is multiplicative, hence Cartier invertible. All iterates have stable rank six or four, giving p-rank and a-number. The Gauss differential equation proves Q_n squarefree, and reciprocity/automorphism classification yield the moduli count. The verifier independently checks exact finite-field matrix identities in five characteristics but is not used to prove the universal statement. Proof boundaries and assumptions appear in RESULT.md.

Elkin establishes general cyclic-cover Cartier rank bounds, and Bouw treats generic cyclic cover p-rank, neither of which implies the exact special-family root polynomial, reducedness, or geometric class count. The closest accessible earlier claim concerns order-eight covers y^4=..., not order-ten y^5=... . Historical priority remains qualified for transformed models and inaccessible literature.

value.rationale: The exact nonordinary locus and p-rank jump of a distinguished moduli family with exceptional automorphisms are natural arithmetic-geometric invariants. For infinitely many primes the theorem classifies all ordinary/nonordinary members, proves a reduced degree-3n divisor, and counts its geometric isomorphism classes. It supplies substantially more information than a generic ordinarity statement, a non-superspeciality test or finite point counts.
